papers.title: What drives the popularity of user-generated derivative videos on video-sharing platforms? Exploring the influence of sentiments in video titles
papers.authors: Li F., Li R., Li S.
papers.abstract: This study investigates how content creators’ sentiments relate to the popularity of derivative videos on online video-sharing platforms. Using a large-scale dataset from Bilibili, China’s leading video-sharing platform, we apply a universal information extraction method to identify sentiments embedded in derivative video titles and analyze their association with video viewership. The results show that derivative videos with critical or negative sentiments are generally associated with higher viewership. Furthermore, this association is moderated by the creator’s social status and institutional endorsements. These findings provide important insights for content creators, platforms, and audiences, highlighting the role of emotional expression in shaping the online popularity of user-generated content.

papers.title: FMCNS: Flow Matching with Causal-aware Negative Sampling for Multimodal Recommendation
papers.authors: Zha X., Zha Y., Jiang H., Song X., Ding H., Dong Y.
papers.abstract: Multimodal recommendation integrates multimodal semantic information of items to model user preferences, where high-quality negative samples are critical for learning discriminative representations. Conventional heuristic methods select negatives based on interaction statistics rather than content semantics, failing to capture fine-grained cross-modal distinctions. Recent diffusion-based approaches generate modality-aware hard negatives but suffer from training instability and overlook exposure bias, where models conflate item visibility with genuine user interest. We propose FMCNS, a framework combining deterministic flow matching with causal intervention for negative sampling. FMCNS constructs straight-line flow trajectories from fused multimodal representations to hard negatives grounded in optimal transport theory, achieving semantically coherent and computationally efficient generation while avoiding noise accumulation inherent in diffusion models. To eliminate spurious correlations from exposure bias, we design a frequency-based causal intervention mechanism that decouples item exposure frequency from user selection probability, adaptively balancing flow-enhanced representations with collaborative embeddings to learn invariant preferences. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets against a wide range of representative baselines demonstrate that FMCNS achieves up to 4.69% and 4.47% improvements in Recall@10 and NDCG@10 over the state-of-the-art methods, while also exhibiting substantial advantages in training efficiency and negative sampling. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaxinji/FMCNS.

papers.title: Is responsible AI a public demand? Trust, risk, and persuasion in local government AI
papers.authors: Senadheera S., Yigitcanlar T., Desouza K., Mossberger K., Cheong P.H., Corchado J., Paz A.
papers.abstract: Local governments are increasingly integrating AI into public service delivery; however, public acceptance remains uneven and is shaped by multiple factors. This study investigates how trust, persuasion, and perceived risk interact to shape public demand for responsible AI. Using a cross-national survey of 1220 respondents across Australia, Spain, and the United States and analysing the data through structural equation modelling (SEM), the study identifies key psychological drivers of public expectations. The findings reveal that trust consistently reduces perceived AI risk, while persuasion primarily strengthens trust rather than directly influencing risk perceptions. Notable cross-country differences emerged; in Australia, trust plays a dominant role in shaping perceptions of AI risk ((Formula presented) ); in Spain, persuasion ((Formula presented) ) balances for low institutional trust; and in the United States, mediated persuasion accounts for nearly 30% of variance in trust ((Formula presented) ). Across all contexts, perceived risk is positively associated with stronger expectations for responsible AI, explaining 11%–24% of the variance in demand. This study contributes by moving beyond normative policy framing of responsible AI and showing empirically that it is a locally interpreted public demand. This highlights that responsible AI is not a universal construct and calls for context-specific strategies that align with local intuitional trust dynamics and mediated persuasive environments.

papers.title: Dynamic cross-instance context mining for multimodal sentiment analysis
papers.authors: Xia H., Cheng Y., Tan Y., Song S.
papers.abstract: Contextual modeling is pivotal in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA). Existing methods primarily rely on an instance-centric paradigm, which focuses on intra-modal dependencies (refining single-modality features) and inter-modal interactions (fusing cross-modality cues) within a single utterance. This isolated approach fails to exploit cross-instance semantic correlations, making models susceptible to local modality noise and incomplete expressions. To bridge this gap, we propose (Formula presented), a framework that shifts the focus from static single-sample fusion to dynamic cross-instance context mining. Our technical highlights are twofold: (i) the Adaptive Context Mining Module (ACMM), which captures cross-instance emotional evolution by retrieving the top-K relevant samples as semantic anchors, effectively increasing the contextual information gain; and (ii) the Heterogeneous Feature Fusion Module (HFFM), which optimizes intra-sample complementarity. Unlike traditional models that treat each utterance independently, (Formula presented) performs utterance-level sentiment prediction enhanced by cross-instance contextual information from semantically related utterances. Experiments on the CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI benchmarks show that (Formula presented) achieves competitive performance, reaching 89.33% and 87.62% Acc-2, respectively. Notably, (Formula presented) outperforms fine-tuned Qwen-1.8B by 3.31% and ChatGLM3-6B by 0.77% in Acc-7, despite a substantially more lightweight architecture. Ablation studies confirm that ACMM and HFFM synergistically enhance contextual representation learning.

papers.title: An intuitionistic fuzzy information processing framework for evaluating crisis communication channels in natural hazard scenarios
papers.authors: Şahin A., Cari M., Kara B., Ayyildiz E.
papers.abstract: To address the complexity of selecting optimal crisis communication channels under information ambiguity, this study develops a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework based on Intuitionistic fuzzy sets to evaluate and rank alternative communication channels under uncertainty. Utilizing data derived from seven domain experts, the model integrates the Best-Worst Method and the Intuitionistic Fuzzy Combinative Distance-based Assessment method to evaluate eight communication strategies against twenty criteria. This approach offers a distinct advantage by mathematically modeling expert hesitation degrees to better capture uncertainty in decision processes. The case study results indicate that timeliness (weight = 0.153) and accuracy (weight = 0.103) are the most critical factors for effective communication. Quantitative rankings identify messaging applications as the most effective strategy, followed by social media platforms, whereas traditional printed materials consistently ranked lowest. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis conducted across five different weighting scenarios confirmed the robustness of digital communication channels as the primary mode of information dissemination. Ultimately, this framework provides policymakers with a structured and intelligent decision support tool to enhance disaster resilience.

papers.title: DualTTrack: Improving information flow consistency in multi-object tracking via dual-track matching and recovery
papers.authors: Li H., Wang Z., Kong W., Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) is a crucial component of intelligent visual information processing systems. Most MOT methods rely on high-confidence detections, while overlooking ambiguous cases, such as noisy false positives or low-confidence true targets, that can disrupt active tracks or hinder track recovery. To address these issues, we propose DualTTrack, a dual-track tracking framework that introduces a potential trajectory pool to buffer and organize uncertain detections. Building on this buffer, we design Dual-Track Matching to prevent interference from low-confidence observations and Dual-Track Recovery to selectively exploit them for reliable reactivation. Our method achieves 65.5 HOTA, 80.7 IDF1, and 82.0 MOTA on MOT17, surpassing BoT-SORT by 1.4% in MOTA. On MOT20, it achieves 63.4 HOTA, 77.6 IDF1, and 78.1 MOTA, with a 1.3% gain in IDF1. On DanceTrack, it reaches 55.8 HOTA, 57.6 IDF1, and 91.6 MOTA. These results demonstrate that buffering low-confidence detections as structured trajectory candidates enhances identity association and strengthens the overall information processing pipeline for tracking.

papers.title: Dynamic valuation of data assets via multi-agent reinforcement learning and Shapley value
papers.authors: Xie S., Hu W., Duan J., Xia Z.
papers.abstract: Accurately valuing data assets is critical for unlocking their economic potential, yet traditional static methods fail to capture their dynamic, context-dependent value. To address this, we propose DSV-MARL, a novel framework that integrates Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with a differentiable dynamic Shapley value mechanism. Each data asset is modeled as an autonomous agent learning to contribute within simulated business environments, while the Shapley approximation enables real-time, interpretable quantification of marginal contributions. Experiments on 3782 real-world data asset records show that DSV-MARL achieves a Spearman correlation of 0.87 with market prices—an improvement of 8.8% over the best baseline—and reduces MSE by 37.3%. The model also demonstrates superior fairness and faster convergence. These results provide a robust, dynamic valuation tool that supports data investment, pricing, and equitable profit-sharing in collaborative data ecosystems.

papers.title: Robust Copyright Verification for Remote Sensing Datasets via Latent Space Embedding
papers.authors: Zhang S., Zhang L., Qiu Y.
papers.abstract: Existing copyright protection for remote sensing datasets is severely limited by the fragility of pixel-domain watermarks against inevitable lossy compression. To address this, we propose LSBI, a compression-resilient latent space backdoor injection framework. This framework constructs triggers via a dual orthogonal projection mechanism and utilizes feature consistency to constrain the embedding position, anchoring the trigger features into compression-robust subspaces to ensure both imperceptibility and robustness. Experimental results on the EuroSAT, PatternNet, and NWPU-RESISC45 datasets demonstrate that LSBI effectively balances imperceptibility, utility, and robustness. Regarding imperceptibility, the method achieves high quantitative visual fidelity with a PSNR exceeding 31 dB and an SSIM above 0.97. In terms of utility, the classifier maintains high clean accuracy with fluctuations generally within approximately 5% as the watermark injection rate increases, indicating efficient decoupling between watermark and original texture features. Regarding robustness, even in black-box scenarios with unknown compression strengths, the method maintains consistent performance across mainstream architectures such as ResNet and VGG. Specifically, under strong compression with a quality factor as low as Q=50, the verification success rate consistently remains above 92%. Moreover, the framework exhibits strong robustness against model fine-tuning and pruning, maintaining success rates exceeding 97% and 92% respectively, providing a robust mechanism for the copyright verification of remote sensing datasets in open environments.

papers.title: Causal deconfounding via multiplex spatial–temporal confounder disentanglement for next POI recommendation
papers.authors: Li J., Wu Z., Dong H., Zheng Z., Lin M.
papers.abstract: Existing next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation methods often struggle to capture the true behavioral mechanisms underlying continuous spatial–temporal transitions, because complex cross-dimensional dependencies and latent confounding effects are insufficiently modeled. To address this issue, we propose DiMuST, a causal deconfounding framework for next POI recommendation. DiMuST characterizes user mobility transitions through a structured causal perspective that distinguishes dimension-specific confounders from joint-dependency confounders. Specifically, a variational multiplex graph autoencoder (VMGAE) is employed to learn proxy representations of different confounders from multiplex spatial–temporal transition graphs, a causal-invariant probabilistic fusion module is designed to recover shared collaborative transition structure, and independence as well as contrastive causal constraints are introduced to purify transition evidence by suppressing spurious correlations. We validated DiMuST on three real-world public datasets NYC, TKY, and CA, which contain between 105,267 and 239,401 check-in records. Compared with advanced models, DiMuST achieved average improvements of about 23.7% and 19.78% in Acc@K and MRR respectively. The experimental results demonstrate that DiMuST can effectively balance independent learning and collaborative verification and generate and interpretable representations.

papers.title: Turning hallucinations into knowledge: Towards identifying clickbait using LLM-generated fallacies
papers.authors: Zhang C., Wang Z., Zhang Z., Zhu Y., Qiang J., Huang Y.
papers.abstract: Knowledge hallucination, commonly known as LLM-generated responses that contain ”false or misleading information” presented as fact, has become one of the spotlight issues in current LLM-related studies, which could be ruinous for discriminative tasks, including clickbait detection. Unlike cutting-edge research that aspires to eliminate the occurrence of ”Hallucinations”, this study attempts to turn LLM hallucinations into known ”false knowledge” instead of treating them as errors. To achieve this goal, we develop a novel supervised LLM reflection-based inference generation method, which allows LLMs to produce both correct (ground-truth) and incorrect (hallucinated) inferences for given news. We then deploy a three-BERT-Encoders-embraced clickbait detection model that conducts contrastive learning for the inferences, as well as the semantic consistency learning between news and inferences. We additionally design a student model via knowledge distillation to avoid the influence of supervised inference production, thereby enabling the model testing to be inference-free. Our experiment results verified on three clickbait datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms four kinds of baselines, including LLM prompting, SLM fine-tuning, and task-specific models across various metrics.

papers.title: Interpretable CNN–KAN hybrid architectures for tabular data with synthetic image encoding
papers.authors: Mondragon-Ruiz G., Liu J., Castillo-Cara M., García-Castro R.
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks excel in vision and language but often struggle with tabular data due to weak inductive biases and limited interpretability. While converting tabular data into synthetic images enables Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to exploit spatial feature interactions, this approach typically exacerbates the models’ black-box nature. To achieve both high predictive power and transparent decision-making, we propose an interpretable Hybrid Neural Network that integrates visual reasoning (CNNs applied to synthetic images) with symbolic learning (Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) applied to tabular data). Extensive evaluations across diverse datasets demonstrate that our CNN–KAN hybrids achieve highly competitive, and often superior, predictive performance. To audit their internal reasoning, we introduce the Global Feature Score (GFS), a unified metric that aggregates spatial saliency from Grad-CAM with symbolic attributions from the KAN branch, producing consistent feature relevance rankings. By explicitly diagnosing modality dominance, layout artifact sensitivity, and inter-branch agreement, the proposed framework significantly reduces reliance on fragile post-hoc methods. Ultimately, embedding interpretability directly into the architecture provides auditable, cross-verified explanations, establishing a robust foundation for Responsible AI-oriented tabular learning.

papers.title: DCEA: A dynamic cognition-emotion aggregation model for interpretable satisfaction prediction with AI conversational services
papers.authors: Xiao H., Zhu T., Wang L., Xu W.
papers.abstract: Enterprises are increasingly deploying AI services, but AI agents may fail to satisfy some users, particularly for those with complicated service requests. It becomes imperative for enterprises to identify these unsatisfied AI services and provide subsequent follow-up by human servers. Current user satisfaction estimation methods predominantly rely on single-dimensional user experience, resulting in suboptimal satisfaction prediction outcomes. This study proposes a theory-driven framework that comprehensively models dynamic multidimensional user experience, enabling interpretable and robust satisfaction prediction with AI services. Specifically, we model user experience from both cognitive and emotional dimensions, and introduce a novel strategy to dynamically reallocate the contributions of user experiences from implicit multi-topic requests toward final satisfaction. An auxiliary task is also designed to identify the reasons for user dissatisfaction, enhancing the interpretability and robustness of user satisfaction prediction. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model, we conduct extensive experiments on three user–AI dialogue datasets derived from real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in predictive performance, especially achieving an average accuracy improvement of 23.91% compared to LLMs. These findings offer valuable theoretical and practical insights for user experience and satisfaction with AI services research.

papers.title: TECP: Insight into hybrid propagation factors from prompt-based LLMs for comprehensive cascade prediction
papers.authors: Zheng J., Wu P., Pan L.
papers.abstract: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future scale of post propagation on social networks. Existing models primarily rely on cascade sequences observed after a specific propagation period, overlooking the intrinsic influence of the text and metadata of source posts on the propagation scale, thereby limiting their ability to provide early-stage predictions and reducing interpretability. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) can extract propagation-related factors by analyzing source post text and metadata, experiments show that they often fail to adaptively select useful insights from these factors. To address these limitations, we propose a Textual Enhanced Cascade Prediction Model based on Large Language Model (TECP). Specifically, TECP utilizes LLMs to analyze the text and metadata of source posts and extract key factors influencing post spread from three aspects rooted in communication theories: topic, content, and audience. To selectively extract meaningful insights from these factors, a Text-Factor Collaboration module is proposed for propagation-aware textual representation. By leveraging multi-task learning, TECP can predict the future cascade level using only textual representations, which can also be seamlessly integrated into existing sequence-based cascade models to predict cascade scale. Experiments on Weibo and Twitter datasets demonstrate the model’s superiority. It achieves a 15.6% higher Macro-F1 for cascade level prediction without relying on cascade sequences. Moreover, as a plug-and-play module, it reduces the average MSLE by 5.24% for sequence-based models in cascade scale prediction. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TECP-DFB9/.

papers.title: From bibliometrics to AI safety: Measuring internal persona disruption in LLMs with the DI-Persona metric
papers.authors: Akbulut M.
papers.abstract: Persona shifts in Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly regarded as a latent safety risk, as they can disrupt internal reasoning pathways in ways that output-based evaluations often fail to detect. In this study, a new metric (DI-Persona) is introduced to quantify internal persona disruption by adapting the bibliometric Disruption Index (DI) to the dense internal representations of Transformer models. DI-Persona is assessed across four distinct model architectures (GPT-2, Qwen2.5–7B, Llama-3.1–8B and Gemma-2–9B) spanning 117M to 9B parameters, using a controlled evaluation suite of 2400 prompts forming 1200 contrastive scenarios across three safety-critical traits: evil, sycophancy, and hallucination. Results show consistent trait-specific disruption patterns across the tested model families. A distinct “hallucination vulnerability” was observed consistently across all four architectures (scores ranging from 0.0019 to 0.0046), suggesting that non-factual generation triggers a consistent restructuring of the model’s latent representations. Conversely, sycophancy exhibited a more model-dependent pattern: scores remained near zero in GPT-2 and Qwen2.5–7B, but were higher in Llama-3.1–8B and Gemma-2–9B. Because model scale, instruction tuning, and model-family differences vary together in the present comparison, this pattern should not be attributed to any one of these factors in isolation. These findings suggest that DI-Persona can be computed consistently across the tested Transformer architectures and may serve as a complementary internal diagnostic signal for persona stability. DI-Persona is presented as a complement to output-based safety evaluations, not as a standalone pre-deployment decision tool. A pilot behavior-linked validation is also reported, relating DI-Persona to harmful compliance, sycophantic agreement, and factual error rates.

papers.title: M2SC2-AD: Multiscale Missing-aware Anomaly Detection framework with scale consistency constraints for sparse multi-sensor
papers.authors: Hu G., Zhou Z., Zhao Y., Dong Z., Li Z., Wu Y., Li Z.
papers.abstract: Multi-sensor time series anomaly detection is critical for ensuring reliability in industrial production and IoT security systems. However, most existing methods are designed for complete data and cannot address missing data caused by communication interruptions and nonuniform sampling. To this end, we propose a Multiscale Missing-aware Anomaly Detection framework with Scale Consistency Constraints for sparse multi-sensor data (M2SC2-AD). Our approach leverages downsampling to generate multiscale series and corresponding missing masks from incomplete Multivariate Time Series (MTS), which are then processed through a novel Multiscale Missing-aware Embedding (MME) module to effectively model missing information. We introduce an Interaction-enhanced Component Decomposition Mixing (ICDM) module to decompose and fuse trend and seasonal components, capturing both long-term trends and cyclical information at each scale. To mitigate the information masking caused by missing values, we propose Scale-consistent Contrastive Learning (SCL), which guides the model to learn scale-invariant representations across different temporal resolutions. The framework is jointly optimized through an Observed Reconstruction Task (ORT) and a Masked Imputation Task (MIT), enabling end-to-end anomaly detection under sparse observation conditions. Extensive experiments on five real-world benchmarks and three additional datasets from distinct application domains demonstrate the superiority of our method. Specifically, M2SC2-AD achieves an average improvement in the F1 score of 2.19% across all benchmarks, and is further validated on the three cross-domain datasets.

papers.title: Mask-enhanced and multi-view aligned heterogeneous graph for text classification
papers.authors: Li J., Sun G., Zhang Z., Wang H.
papers.abstract: Text classification serves as a fundamental task in natural language processing, with widespread applications across multiple domains. Nevertheless, The existing sequence based methods have the problem of semantic isolation, and the graph neural network based methods have the problems of noise sensitivity and rough multi-source information fusion mechanism. To address these shortcomings, we introduce a Mask-Enhanced and Multi-View Aligned Heterogeneous Graph (MEMVAHG) method for text classification. First, three heterogeneous graphs: word–document graph, document–label graph and word–document–label graph, are systematically constructed to comprehensively model semantic relationships. Subsequently, graph augmentation strategy is incorporated into a graph encoder–decoder framework to enhance model robustness. Finally, a multi-view feature alignment mechanism is designed, where the distribution of document representations obtained from different graph decoders is constrained through the minimization of Maximum Mean Discrepancy loss, thereby achieving deep semantic collaboration. Multiple comparative experiments on 5 benchmark datasets demonstrate that, compared to the best baseline results on each dataset, MEMVAHG achieves improvements of at least 0.0167, 0.0151, 0.0138 and 0.0204 in Accuracy, Precision, micro-F1 and macro-F1 respectively across all datasets, demonstrating its consistent superiority and robust performance. The main code is available at https://github.com/sgysgywaityou/MEMVAHG.

papers.title: ECO-SFL: Efficient collaborative Split Federated Learning for mitigating stragglers via resource heterogeneity in IoT devices
papers.authors: Guo C., Sun H., Li X., Tang X., Jie Y.
papers.abstract: Split Federated Learning (SFL) enables resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices to participate in training large-scale deep neural networks by leveraging the server’s computational capabilities. However, the inclusion of these devices introduces severe latency bottlenecks caused by slower participants (known as stragglers), which forces an unsustainable reliance on the server for workload offloading. This, in turn, leads to excessive server-side resource consumption and processing congestion, even interrupting the overall training process. To address these challenges, we introduce ECO-SFL, an efficient collaborative SFL framework that uniquely transforms resource heterogeneity from a performance barrier into a driving force for reducing latency and increasing the system’s tolerance to stragglers. Specifically, we design a Layer-wise Collaborative Strategy (LCS) that dynamically forms teams by pairing high-performance “helper” clients with resource-constrained “recipient” clients, utilizing helpers’ idle time while waiting for server updates to process recipients’ residual workloads, thereby significantly reducing latency. To enable optimal team formation and workload allocation, we design a lightweight Roofline-based time estimation method that allows the server to predict each client’s layer-wise processing latency locally without imposing extra computation or model loading on clients. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed ECO-SFL effectively mitigates the straggler problem while maintaining accuracy and convergence performance. Especially under the hardware disparity configuration, ECO-SFL demonstrates significant advantages on ResNet-152, reducing system latency by more than 90% compared to baseline methods.

papers.title: IMGSL: Citation-based Innovation Motif Graph Structure Learning for scholar profiling
papers.authors: Huang J., Ai M., Li X., Bu Y., Jia T.
papers.abstract: Scientific research is inherently cumulative, as new achievements are often inspired by prior contributions, built upon them, and recombined with existing knowledge. Identifying structural patterns underlying such cumulative knowledge development is a key challenge in scholar profiling and expert finding. In this paper, we define a set of citation-based Innovation Motifs, including the Giant Motif, to characterize higher-order patterns of citation evolution in scientific citation networks and to model how prior knowledge is repeatedly inherited and extended in scholars’ research trajectories. Based on large-scale real-world citation data spanning seven computer science subfields and 3500 scholar profiles, we empirically show that these motif structures exhibit systematic differences between awardees and non-awardees. Leveraging this observation, we construct Giant Motif-enhanced citation subgraphs and propose an Innovation Motif Graph Structure Learning (IMGSL) framework to learn scholar representations. We evaluate IMGSL on multiple real-world datasets through downstream tasks such as scholar award prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art graph neural network baselines, achieving up to a 3.61% performance improvement in the NLP field. Comprehensive analyses further demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and interpretability of IMGSL, showing that motif-enhanced structural representations provide useful evidence for characterizing scholars’ long-term research trajectories.

papers.title: Disentangling relational semantics in graph data to summarize entity descriptions
papers.authors: Yang J., Liu Z., Li Z., Wu L., Hu H., Wang H., Zhao H.
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs), despite their widespread applications, suffer from severe information overload. Entity Summarization (ES) has emerged as a crucial technique to mitigate this issue. However, existing methods typically formulate ES as an item-wise ranking problem, where each description is evaluated largely in isolation. Such formulations are limited in capturing set-level complementarity, especially when a summary is expected to cover multiple semantic aspects. In this paper, we model summary complementarity as relations induced by latent semantic preference factors among descriptions. From this perspective, a high-quality summary is not merely a collection of individually salient descriptions, but a coherent set whose members reflect distinct yet mutually supportive semantic aspects. To this end, we propose the Disentangled Relational Summarizer (DRS), a novel approach that frames ES as an explicit link prediction task. DRS is built upon a graph-based neural architecture that learns disentangled representations to explicitly model the multifaceted semantic preferences between descriptions. Furthermore, a composite loss mechanism is introduced to maintain the diversity of description representations, counteracting representational collapse during message passing. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that DRS achieves strong overall performance, improving average F1 scores over the strongest baselines by 7.2% and 12.2%, and achieving the best Property Coverage result in five of six settings with a 5.0% average PC improvement over the strongest baseline.

papers.title: A multi-expert adaptive framework for test-time personalization in federated learning
papers.authors: Guo S., Chen Z., Li C., Zhang Y., Zhang X.
papers.abstract: The heterogeneity of client data (i.e., non-IID distributions) in federated learning (FL) limits the generalization ability of global models across diverse test datasets. To address this challenge, we propose FedMEA (Multi-expert federated adaptive learning), which clusters clients into groups to distill expert models and dynamically integrates their predictions through self-supervised ensemble strategies. This design improves robustness to previously unseen data distributions with a controllable overhead confined to the Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) phase, while preserving standard inference efficiency after adaptation. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed FedMEA, we conducted extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets. FedMEA consistently outperformed state-of-the-art federated learning methods. Specifically, compared with FedAvg and FedProx, FedMEA improved average global accuracy by 26.3% and 26.5%, respectively, while maintaining competitive personalized performance on local datasets, demonstrating its robustness and scalability in handling client data heterogeneity. Further analyses confirm its superior performance from multiple perspectives.

papers.title: Asynchrony as information: Predicting technology transfer opportunities through science–technology knowledge lag
papers.authors: Yu Y., Wu J., Shui D., Dong X.
papers.abstract: Predicting technology transfer opportunities bridges the gap between science and technology (S&T) knowledge discoveries and industrial applications. Constrained by the perspective of single technology transfers, prior studies cannot capture the temporal evolution of technology transfer opportunities at the industry level. Furthermore, they overlook S&T asynchrony, which signifies more than a temporal delay and embodies forward-looking commercial potential of technology. To address this, this paper proposes a prediction framework that operationalizes S&T knowledge lag to represent this asynchrony. First, to resolve terminological discrepancies between S&T knowledge, we construct a sub-technology list and fine-tune an LLM to map knowledge texts to unified sub-technologies, achieving semantic alignment. Subsequently, we construct temporal co-occurrence networks for S&T knowledge and employ time-lag cross-correlation to quantify the temporal knowledge lag between sub-technologies as an implicit network attribute. Finally, we design a graph-based dual-stream attention mechanism with a gated fusion strategy to integrate this implicit lag attribute with the explicit transfer structure. This mechanism adaptively balances the structural and attribute streams, enabling accurate and interpretable prediction. Experiments on an AI dataset demonstrate that the model exhibits superior performance in 1-step, 3-step, and 5-step ahead predictions, achieving F1-score improvements of 1.6%, 2.3%, and 6.88%, respectively, over the best benchmark model. Crucially, the value of S&T knowledge lag becomes increasingly pronounced as the prediction step extends. This model empowers the industry to proactively anticipate technological evolution and identify commercially viable opportunities.

papers.title: Detecting market manipulation with dual-branch self-supervised learning: A unified framework integrating frequency-informed anomaly synthesis and domain-specific features
papers.authors: Dai Y., Quinn B., Kearney F., Liu W., Spence I., Rafferty K., Wang H.
papers.abstract: Effective detection of financial market manipulation is critically impeded by three fundamental challenges: signal concealment, data sparsity, the boundary vagueness. This paper introduces SD-FMM, a Self-supervised Detection framework tailored for Financial Market Manipulation that addresses these fundamental challenges through three innovative components. First, our Amplification Component extracts and fuses domain-specific features grounded in market microstructure theory, substantially amplifying subtle manipulation signals that would otherwise remain concealed. Second, our Synthesis Component generates realistic synthetic anomalies through few-shot learning and dynamic frequency analysis using Discrete Wavelet Transform, enabling self-supervised training without relying on scarce labeled data. Third, our Detection Component employs a novel Dual-branch Contrastive Detection Neural Network that enhances sensitivity to manipulation boundaries through local contrastive learning and holistic modeling of temporal dependency. We evaluate SD-FMM using a newly collected proprietary dataset of 25 Chinese stock market manipulation cases and a public benchmark of 338 cryptocurrency pump-and-dump schemes. Extensive experiments against 12 state-of-the-art baselines demonstrate the significant superiority of SD-FMM. On the stock dataset, our method outperforms the second-best baseline by 47.61% in average precision metrics and reduces the false alarm rate by 47.46%. Meanwhile, it shortens the mean detection delay by 25.05%, enabling swift regulatory intervention. On the cryptocurrency dataset, SD-FMM exhibits remarkable sensitivity, achieving a Hit Rate@3 of 83.13% and Hit Rate@20 of 97.93%. Overall, our framework offers a generalized solution that can not only accurately distinguish manipulations from normal trading but also deliver a faster and stronger response to manipulations across diverse financial markets.

papers.title: A multi-scale spatio-temporal dynamic graph neural network for airborne network intrusion detection
papers.authors: Liu W., Zhou M., Gao C., Ge H.
papers.abstract: Intrusion detection systems are a core component of airborne network security. Traditional machine learning approaches usually rely on fixed time-domain sliding windows for feature extraction, which results in limited receptive fields. To address the robustness limitations of convolutional neural networks that depend on such windowing mechanisms, this paper proposes a multi-scale perspective convolution module. In this module, perspective parameters and learnable parameters are configured across multiple scales to comprehensively capture airborne network communication patterns. To further capture the complex and dynamic spatial features of network traffic, a collaborative spatio-temporal learning framework is proposed, integrating a time-domain causal convolutional network with a spatial-domain dynamic graph neural network. Experimental results on the MIL-STD-1553 and CICIDS2017 airborne network datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 99% detection accuracy with low false alarm rates. Compared with the state-of-the-art baseline methods, the proposed method shows superior detection performance and strong potential for practical deployment.

papers.title: Labels matter: Incorporating label knowledge into dual branch knowledge distillation framework for long-tailed ICD code assignment
papers.authors: Cai L., Niu H., Lv H., Liu W., Wang Z., Liu Y., Ren P.
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based automated International Classification of Diseases (ICD) code assignment is essential and valuable task for modern healthcare systems. However, due to the long-tailed distribution of ICD codes, the data-driven deep learning-based approaches perform poorly on rare diseases. To address this challenge, we propose a novel dual-branch knowledge distillation (DBKD) framework that explicitly incorporates label knowledge for long-tailed ICD code assignment. The proposed framework introduces two key innovations: (1) the joint integration of label semantics, label hierarchy and label co-occurrence to enhanced feature learning and classifier learning, and (2) a dual-branch knowledge distillation strategy that balances discriminative feature learning with less-biased classifier learning. We evaluate DBKD on publicly available datasets MIMIC-III and a private Chinese electronic medical record dataset, used solely as an external validation to assess generalization. Experimental results demonstrate that DBKD achieves competitive performance and superior generalization capability in long-tailed learning scenario. Further interpretability analysis highlights credibility and clinical utility of our proposed method. The source code and related dataset are available at https://github.com/Cai-Linkun/DBKD.

papers.title: An LLM-assisted decision-support system for semantic analysis of Bloom’s Taxonomy-aligned learning outcomes
papers.authors: Gültekin A., Diri S., Özcan M.
papers.abstract: This study presents a Large Language Model (LLM)–assisted decision-support system to help higher-education instructors write course learning outcomes (CLOs) aligned with Bloom’s Taxonomy. The system is primarily based on GPT-4o, while additional language models were employed for comparative and evaluative purposes. The system was tested in practice with 22 faculty members across different departments. Following use of the system, usability and user perceptions were examined using the System Usability Scale, which yielded an average score of 79.64 (SD = 13.33), well above the accepted threshold of 68; 80.95% of participants rated the system as having a high level of usability. In parallel, qualitative analysis of open-ended faculty responses identified five dominant themes through manual thematic coding, capturing perceptions related to Bloom’s alignment, user experience, expectation fulfillment, institutional quality assurance, and system dissemination. To further triangulate these manually derived themes, Latent Dirichlet Allocation was employed as a complementary analytical technique. Subsequently, the generated CLOs were evaluated by three subject-matter experts with extensive teaching experience. Quantitative analyses indicated that LLM-assisted CLOs received higher average expert ratings for alignment with Bloom’s Taxonomy (M = 4.60) compared to instructor-written CLOs (M = 3.64) with statistically significant differences (p < 0.001). Beyond participant perceptions, inter-rater reliability analyses highlighted the inherently interpretive and criterion-dependent nature of evaluations based on Bloom’s Taxonomy. Agreement levels varied substantially across evaluation dimensions. Expert consensus was limited for conceptually abstract criteria, particularly alignment with Bloom’s Taxonomy, whereas stronger agreement was observed for linguistic clarity and aspects related to measurability. Accordingly, observed mean score differences for criteria exhibiting low or near-zero inter-rater reliability may be interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. Thus, these findings frame the system’s contribution not as enforcing uniform expert agreement, but rather as supporting clearer, more operationally defined learning outcomes. In this respect, the results suggest that LLMs can function as effective decision-support systems for enhancing the clarity, measurability, and usability of CLOs, thereby supporting curriculum design and quality assurance processes in higher education.

papers.title: Densifying Knowledge Hypergraphs with LLM-based review distillation for conversational consumer decision support
papers.authors: Jin K., Zhang Y., Blanco-Encomienda F.J.
papers.abstract: Conversational recommender systems (CRS) support consumer decision making through multi-turn dialogue, but their effectiveness is often limited by sparse conversational supervision and incomplete structural knowledge. Consumer reviews contain rich item-level evidence about attributes, styles, and preference rationales, yet directly injecting raw reviews into CRS models may introduce noise and does not provide reusable relational structure. To address this issue, we propose RD-HGCR, a review-driven hypergraph framework for conversational recommendation. RD-HGCR first distills compact item-level semantics from reviews with an LLM, grounds the distilled concepts to canonical knowledge-graph entities, and then adds these entities to item-centric hyperedges. Based on the densified hypergraph, the model learns shared item representations for both recommendation and response generation. A decoupled two-stage training strategy further aligns hypergraph representations with review-derived semantics before conversational fine-tuning. Experiments on ReDIAL and TG-REDIAL demonstrate statistically significant improvements over strong baselines on both recommendation accuracy and response generation quality. Human evaluation further confirms that RD-HGCR produces more informative, relevant, and coherent responses. Additional analyses on frequency-stratified item groups show that the gains are especially pronounced on low-frequency items, while a computational-overhead study confirms that LLM-based review distillation is a one-time offline preprocessing step with manageable cost. Overall, the results highlight the importance of converting review evidence into reusable structure for robust conversational decision support.

papers.title: A synergistic causal-driven two-stage hierarchical adaptive integration paradigm with breakpoint segmentation for carbon price prediction
papers.authors: Li Y., Pan Y., Chen J.
papers.abstract: Accurate carbon price prediction is crucial for the global low‑carbon transition, yet non-stationarity and structural changes pose challenges. Validated on two Chinese carbon markets and the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), this study proposes a framework to address limitations of existing models in handling data breaks, causal insight and adaptability. It first employs a segmentation-guided multi-scale feature extraction (SG-MSFE) technique, which can detect breakpoints and capture multi-frequency components per segment. DoWhy causal inference technique then filters key external drivers for these components. From a diverse pool, optimal base models are selected per component using a noise-injected scoring mechanism balancing accuracy and stability. A hierarchical ensemble strategy is applied: Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) integrates component predictions locally for each segment, forming independent ensemble models. Then Q-learning dynamically assigns weights globally to these models for the final prediction, adapting to real-time market dynamics. This design enhances interpretability through segmentation context, explainable causal drivers, transparent model selection, and dynamic weights revealing market regime relevance. In the Hubei market, the framework achieved mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.0624, 0.1293, 0.5381%. Outperforming other advanced models, it shows superior forecasting and potential for broader applicability.

papers.abstract: Liver cancer requires accurate imaging, therapy, and follow-up for early and precise diagnosis. Computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data are commonly used in AI-assisted computer-aided diagnostics to support this effort. However, tumor size and structural variability often challenge effective segmentation of affected regions. To address this, we propose the Transformer Attention Network Optimized Segmentation (TANOS) approach, which integrates a transformer with a morphological attention network to accurately identify tumor boundaries and assess structural pattern changes. The model was validated using strict patient-level partitioning with zero data leakage: LiTS (130 patients; 91 training / 20 validation / 19 test), 3DIRCADb (20 patients; 14 training / 3 validation / 3 test), and Pancreas-CT (80 patients; auxiliary cross-organ training only - no evaluation metrics computed on this dataset), covering individuals aged 18 to 76.Experimental results show that TANOS improves segmentation performance compared to current methods, achieving 13.63% higher accuracy and 13.11% higher precision, along with a 13.88% reduction in false rate. These findings demonstrate that TANOS is a reliable tool for enhancing clinical diagnostic performance and liver tumor segmentation accuracy, with consistent results across all experiments and evaluations.

papers.title: Graph-prompted explainable fake news detection with multimodal large language models
papers.authors: Zhou Y., Li P., Han K., Cheng S.
papers.abstract: As online news increasingly evolves into multimodal content, the rapid development of social media has intensified the spread of fake news, making multimodal fake news detection an important research problem. However, existing methods often fail to effectively leverage structural and textual information in propagation graphs, and they also suffer from limited knowledge coverage and weak information integration, which leads to poor interpretability and generalization. To address these issues, we propose a Graph Prompt-Augmented Multimodal (GPAM) framework for fake news detection. GPAM integrates textual content, visual evidence, and propagation structures by combining pretrained large vision-language models with graph neural networks. Specifically, we encode rumor propagation structures as soft prompts and transform structured user comments into hard prompts, enabling the model to jointly reason over multimodal and structural signals. Extensive experiments on the Pheme and Weibo benchmark datasets demonstrate strong performance, improving over current state-of-the-art multimodal methods by approximately 1.2% and 3.6%, respectively. Moreover, our model exhibits superior generalization, reducing performance degradation by over 20 percentage points in cross-dataset transfer settings, and delivers more faithful and informative explanations, achieving 17%–24% higher quality scores than existing LVLM-based approaches.

papers.title: An explainable ensemble learning approach for financial fraud detection: Integrating SHAP and LIME on the PaySim dataset
papers.authors: Gamal N., Younis E.M.G., Mohamed W.M.
papers.abstract: Credit card fraud detection requires highly accurate and interpretable models to minimize financial losses and build trust in automated systems. Although machine learning models achieve high predictive accuracy, their deployment is often hindered by class imbalance, computational efficiency, and interpretability challenges. Many existing studies overlook precision–recall performance under extreme imbalance, computational burden, and explanation reliability. This study addresses these challenges using the PaySim dataset, which simulates mobile money transactions with extreme class imbalance. The research investigates four core dimensions: SMOTE for imbalance mitigation, explainable AI (XAI) methods using SHAP and LIME for interpretability, learning-curve analysis for data sufficiency insights, and computational cost assessment reflecting real-time system constraints. Multiple advanced ensemble models were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, including AdaBoostClassifier with RandomForestClassifier and a StackingClassifier combining ExtraTrees, AdaBoost variants, and XGBoost. A dual-strategy framework is proposed: StackingClassifier as the primary model when computational resources are available, and AdaBoostClassifier with RandomForest as an efficient alternative for resource-constrained environments. Both models were evaluated under two operational scenarios: post-transaction and real-time fraud detection. In post-transaction scenarios, the StackingClassifier achieved 99.99% accuracy, 0.9999 F1 score, 0.9999 precision, 1.0 recall, and 0.9999 AUC, while AdaBoostClassifier achieved 99.99% accuracy, 0.9999 F1 score, 0.9998 precision, 1.0 recall, and 1.0 AUC. In real-time scenarios (excluding balance-related features unavailable during live processing), both maintained superior performance despite feature reduction. Comprehensive analysis on AdaBoostClassifier with RandomForest demonstrated consistent, interpretable explanations and computational efficiency. The study offers a resource-aware framework balancing accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability across different operational contexts.

papers.title: Similarity-aware feature calibration stabilizes low-contrast and missing-modality brain segmentation
papers.authors: Zhou M., Cheng M., Yang L., Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Reliable fusion of heterogeneous MRI sources for brain tumor segmentation remains difficult under misalignment, incomplete protocols, and weak local contrast. We study a recurrent instability in U shaped encoder decoder networks where skip features are fused without verifying semantic consistency, which can inject semantic noise and trigger prediction collapse in low contrast regions. We propose a similarity aware calibration framework that replaces passive skip fusion with reliability conditioned feature propagation. A non local adaptive prior provides anatomy-consistent prior features via variational reconstruction, and a similarity weighted gating module uses local normalized cross correlation to suppress inconsistent skip information in a scale invariant manner. A contrast enhanced region attention module amplifies faint boundary evidence to mitigate gradient starvation in fuzzy transitions. On BraTS 2019, 2021, and 2023 validation benchmarks, NAP SCAF achieves average Dice scores of 94.14%, 96.05%, and 96.74%, respectively. On BraTS 2023, it improves average Dice by 6.73 points and reduces average HD95 by 4.19 mm relative to HFF Net. The framework mitigates collapse failures by reducing extreme Hausdorff outliers above 150 mm to values around 10 mm, and it remains robust under missing modality settings, achieving 93.79% average Dice across 14 modality subsets and 92.16% with a single modality on BraTS 2021. papers.title: A benchmark framework for detecting cyberbullying: Conceptual and operational definitions, dataset development, and methods evaluation
papers.authors: Yang X., Lv W., Reusens M., Zhang B., Baesens B.
papers.abstract: Cyberbullying detection is vital for maintaining public order online. Yet the lack of standardized benchmark frameworks makes it difficult for datasets and models to reflect cyberbullying’s essential attributes. In particular, many studies focus only on classifying content as aggressive or non-aggressive while overlooking other dimensions, a problem that has long received insufficient attention. To fill this gap, this study introduces a new benchmark framework for cyberbullying detection, covering conceptual and operational definitions, dataset development, and methods evaluation. Specifically, this study: (1) proposes conceptual and operational definitions that reflect the four core characteristics of cyberbullying: targeting, aggression, repetition, and harmfulness; (2) publicly releases a relatively large-scale Chinese Multimodal Cyberbullying dataset (texts with emojis) that strictly follows the definition of cyberbullying and can reflect its core characteristics, containing 20,211 annotated instances; and (3) provides results for eight baseline methods covering classical machine learning, encoder-based and decoder-based Large Language models (LLMs). The results show that BERT trained on the developed dataset achieves the best overall performance. In terms of PRAUC, BERT surpasses the second-best LR method by 13.88%, and outperforms the 10-shot instruction-optimized Qwen2.5-7B and DeepSeek-V3.2 by 23.61% and 20.6%, respectively. Attention and SHAP analyses further indicate that BERT effectively captures cyberbullying characteristics and offers interpretability. The framework standardizes definitions, characteristics, data collection and splitting, and evaluation metrics and protocols, while allowing flexible design for harmfulness specification and event selection. papers.title: Cross-sectional analysis of large language models in current natural language generation challenges
papers.authors: Maestre M.M., Martínez-Murillo I., Martínez A.M., Lloret E.
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) has produced diverse model families with multiple versions differing in parameter size and release chronology. While this ongoing progress has driven substantial advancements in Natural Language Generation (NLG), several critical challenges remain unmet. This paper presents a cross-sectional analysis of 24 model versions from five prominent LLM families, evaluating their performance across five persistent generation gaps. For each gap, we define three targeted tasks to systematically assess model behaviour, with three prompt variants per task to analyse them with comprehensive examples, yielding 45 distinct prompts and 1080 model responses.Human expert qualitative analysis reveals that gpt-4o and gpt-40-mini accurately respond to 75.5% and 46.6% of prompts respectively, while models as llama-3.2-3b-instruct and llama-3.2-1b-instruct achieve only 11% and 10% accuracy respectively. Our study also highlights a key and unexpected insight: in several cases, earlier or smaller LLM versions sometimes match or exceed the performance of their latest, larger counterparts. These findings invite a timely discussion within the NLG community about the current trajectory of scaling models versus focusing on the optimisation and adaptation of existing architectures. We hope this analysis contributes valuable perspectives for more informed and strategic development of future LLMs in the field of NLG.

papers.abstract: Metaphor recognition is a challenging task in natural language processing (NLP) due to the subtle semantic nuances and dynamic contextual features of metaphors, which existing methods fail to fully capture. To address this issue, we propose a Ternary Paradigm-Driven and Dual-Framework Semantic Interaction model (TPTSI) for metaphor recognition. Specifically, we design a ternary paradigm construction module that combines positive examples, anchor sentences and negative examples to excavate the metaphorical features of sentences in depth. We also develop a Dual-Framework Semantic Interaction Module integrating Selectional Preference Violation (SPV) and Metaphor Identification Procedure (MIP) to assess the semantic fit and deviation of target words in sentence contexts, enhancing the model’s understanding of metaphorical semantic structures. Extensive experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets with distinct scales and characteristics: MOH-X (1849 target words, 1702 sentences), TroFi (4387 target words, 4269 sentences) and VUA-20 (189,008 target words, 16,506 sentences). TPTSI significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines, yielding 1.4%, 2.4% and 4.5% F1-score improvements on the MOH-X, TroFi and VUA-20 datasets respectively. Ablation experiments further validate the indispensability of each core component, with the ternary paradigm construction module leading to up to 25.9%, 3.6% and 12.8% F1-score gains on the MOH-X, TroFi and VUA-20 datasets respectively.

papers.title: Collective-level propagation analysis via LLM-enhanced hypergraph transformer for fake news detection
papers.authors: Wei S., Wu B., Zhou T., Liu X., Tan J., Liu D., Su G.
papers.abstract: Fake news detection is crucial for safeguarding information security and maintaining social stability. Existing studies use graph neural networks to capture news propagation features to boost fake news detection. However, constrained by the pairwise nature of conventional graphs, they decompose propagation into a set of individual-level behaviors. In practice, news diffusion is a collective propagation process rather than a simple aggregation of individual behaviors. Real and fake news exhibit distinct collective propagation behavior patterns, which can provide valuable cues for fake news detection. To exploit such collective-level characteristics, we propose LeHT, an LLM-enhanced hypergraph transformer framework for fake news detection via collective-level propagation analysis. LeHT leverages a large language model as a context provider to generate context-enhanced semantic representations, alleviating semantic sparsity in short news posts and enabling better understanding of semantics that may trigger collective reactions. Meanwhile, we construct propagation hypergraphs to explicitly model collective propagation behaviors, where each news item is represented as a hyperedge connecting all participating users. Based on the propagation hypergraph and the context-enhanced semantic representations, we design a hypergraph transformer network with a three-level attention mechanism to capture complex higher-order correlations in collective propagation behaviors and learn discriminative collective propagation behavior pattern representations for fake news detection. Experiments on three public datasets — Twitter (1152 news items), PHEME (1705 news items), and DRWeibo (6037 news items) — demonstrate that LeHT achieves ACC/F1 scores of 0.923/0.921, 0.926/0.924, and 0.916/0.913, respectively.

To address these challenges, we propose a multiscale adaptive spectral–spatial dual-path attention network (MASSANet), which employs a spectral branch for multi-scale frequency pattern extraction, a spatial branch for discriminative electrode-related representation learning, and an attention-based fusion strategy to adaptively integrate complementary information. This design reduces the dependence on manual frequency-band selection and improves the robustness of MI-EEG decoding across different recording conditions. The proposed method is evaluated on three public benchmark datasets, including BCI Competition IV 2a, BCI Competition IV 2b, and OpenBMI. Experimental results show that MASSANet achieves classification accuracies of 74.46%/84.07%, 88.38%/88.85%, and 65.50%/87.09% under cross-session and within-session conditions, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness across different MI-EEG decoding scenarios. papers.title: DADSA: Dual-Side Adaptive Deep Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.authors: Li K., Peng Y., Zhou C., Zhang F., Ma J., Qiao Y., Huang W., Wang X.
papers.abstract: Most existing safety alignment methods for large language models (LLMs) constrain only the initial tokens of generation. However, safety signals decay with generation depth and these methods lack adaptivity in capturing deep-level unsafe signals. To tackle these issues, we propose Dual-Side Adaptive Deep Safety Alignment (DADSA), a deep safety alignment framework that adaptively models both generation depth and constraint strength. First, we extend existing safety benchmarks by constructing SafetyPre and HarmSafetyPre, comprising 510 instructions and 510 instruction–response pairs across 17 harmful categories, respectively, to support adaptive deep alignment. Furthermore, we develop a dual-track data regime that balances safety and utility. Second, we propose Adaptive Curriculum Safety Augmentation (ACSA), which combines adaptive risk-aware depth sampling based on token level refusal probabilities with a curriculum depth scheduler, gradually guiding the model from shallow refusal patterns to robust defenses over long contexts and harmful semantic regions. Third, we present Adaptive-γ Soft-Constrained Fine-Tuning (Aγ[jls-end-space/]-SFT), which adaptively adjusts token-level constraint strength as a function of generation position and safety deviation, yielding an optimization paradigm that is stable while preserving shallow safety and enforcing strong deep level refusal. Extensive experiments on mainstream LLMs show that ACSA lowers attack success rate by 21.86% under GCG attacks, and Aγ[jls-end-space/]-SFT lowers attack success rate by 51.27% under fine-tuning attacks.

papers.title: Hint-oriented self-suggestive learning for commonsense information processing
papers.authors: Fan Y., Zou B., Li Y., Hong Y.
papers.abstract: Multi-Choice Commonsense Question Answering (MC-CQA) is an important component of cognitive information science, particularly for advancing the reasoning functions of information systems. However, effective information processing for reasoning remains difficult. Distractors are often plausible when models lack relevant knowledge or explicit guidance. This article presents Hint-Oriented Representation Learning (HORL), an effective and integrated framework designed to synergize internal and external hints for enhanced reasoning. Within this framework, internal hints are formalized as structured intent descriptors, while external hints consist of expert-like advice simulating human knowledge acquisition to delineate correct and incorrect inferential paths. Specifically, HORL implements a dual-task learning paradigm: a keyword prediction task for intent internalization, and a contrastive learning task that optimizes information representations by aligning them with expert-guided pattern. Through this approach, the framework simulates a self-suggestion mechanism during training, effectively internalizing the reasoning patterns derived from both internal hints and external expertise into the model’s latent space. To evaluate the system’s decision-support robustness, we employ RoBERTa, ELECTRA, Flan-T5, and LLaMA as backbone models and evaluate HORL on the CODAH and Discosense benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that HORL consistently outperforms baseline methods. By leveraging external advice from GPT-5, HORL achieves accuracy improvements of 5.58% and 3.52% on CODAH and Discosense, respectively. Furthermore, HORL surpasses state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) in both Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and zero/few-shot settings. This framework provides an effective way to integrate internal and external hints into reasoning models. Our findings offer practical insights for developing knowledge-enhanced intelligent systems.

papers.title: Attribution-driven background modeling network with context-aware anomaly suppression for hyperspectral anomaly detection
papers.authors: Wang C., Huo Y., Zhang M., Ren J., Wang H.
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to identify pixels whose spectral signatures deviate from the surrounding background without requiring prior knowledge. Although autoencoder-based methods achieve promising performance, they often suffer from insufficient separation between background and anomalous samples and inadequate modeling of heterogeneous background patterns. Moreover, the strong representation capability of neural networks may cause certain anomalies to be reconstructed, resulting in missed detections. To address these limitations, we propose an attribution-driven background modeling network with context-aware anomaly suppression, termed ADANet. The proposed framework adaptively mines sample attributions, explicitly models diverse background patterns, and suppresses anomaly reconstruction. Specifically, we develop a feature-guided sample attribution mining (FGSAM) strategy that leverages representative background prototypes to infer sample attributions, enabling effective separation of multiple background categories and reliable identification of anomalies. Building on this, a spectral-feature consistent discriminative (SFCD) loss is designed to enforce intra-class compactness and inter-class separability among background features, while maintaining structural consistency between the spectral and feature domains. In addition, we propose a context-aware anomaly suppression (CAAS) module that leverages background features from the spatial neighborhoods of anomalous pixels to constrain anomaly reconstruction, driving reconstructed anomalies toward the background distribution and thereby reducing missed detections. Quantitative comparisons with state-of-the-art methods show that our approach achieves consistently high (Formula presented) values across six hyperspectral image datasets, with the highest value reaching 99.95%, and outperforms the second-best method by up to 0.70%. Qualitative comparisons further support the superiority of the proposed method.

papers.title: EvoFlow: A closed-loop first-order optimizer for stable and robust deep learning
papers.authors: Khan Z., Shen Y., Liu H.
papers.abstract: Robust and efficient optimization remains a central challenge in deep learning as widely used first-order methods are often sensitive to learning-rate selection and noisy or non-stationary gradients. This paper proposes EvoFlow, an (Formula presented) first-order optimizer that introduces closed-loop update regulation through cosine-adaptive momentum with a momentum floor, alignment-based step amplification, and trust-aware suppression driven by inter-iteration gradient change. These mechanisms are designed to improve stability and reduce tuning sensitivity without costly second-order approximations or perturbation-based updates. Under bounded-preconditioner and momentum-tracking assumptions, the analysis establishes non-convex convergence at the standard first-order rate (Formula presented) and derives stability bounds for the adaptive momentum and suppression terms. Experiments across vision, language understanding, generative modeling, and language modeling tasks show that EvoFlow is competitive with strong baselines under a unified tuning budget. Across CIFAR, GLUE, ImageNet-1K, and robustness benchmarks, EvoFlow demonstrates statistically supported improvements in selected settings and competitive performance in others, with effect sizes interpreted in relation to cross-seed variability where repeated trials are available. In GAN training, EvoFlow provides balanced generator–discriminator optimization and stable FID/KID trajectories. Under the tested WikiText-2 language-modeling protocol, EvoFlow obtains the lowest evaluation loss and perplexity on GPT-2, Pythia-1B, and GPT-Neo, while incurring higher resource costs than some throughput-optimized baselines. The results suggest that EvoFlow offers a theoretically grounded and practically implementable framework for feedback-regulated first-order optimization in stable deep learning.

papers.title: Fine-grained sequential recommendation with prototype-level individualized opinion adjustment
papers.authors: Wang X., Zheng J., Liao J., Xing X., Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Current review-based sequential recommendations typically leverage item attribute content to infer user interest for next-item prediction. However, due to the semantic complexity of review texts, existing approaches often struggle to accurately capture fine-grained individualized opinion biases in user behaviors. To address this limitation, we propose POARec, a fine-grained sequential recommendation framework based on prototype-level individualized opinion adjustment. POARec leverages an LLM-based agent to extract fine-grained attribute-opinion pairs from raw reviews, enabling the construction of comprehensive and interpretable user and item opinion profiles. Building on these profiles, the framework introduces a prototype-guided opinion adjustment mechanism to learn group-level attribute prototypes. These prototypes are used to calibrate semantic noise and alleviate sparsity in individual opinion representations to model fine-grained attribute-aware sequence embeddings for next-item prediction. We evaluated POARec on four real-world datasets, Amazon Sports, Amazon Beauty, Amazon Clothing, and Yelp. Experimental results show that POARec improves Hit@10 and NDCG@10 by 3.03% and 14.95% on the Sports dataset, 4.86% and 6.93% on the Beauty dataset, 7.72% and 11.42% on the Clothing dataset, and 9.03% and 4.84% on the Yelp dataset, respectively. Furthermore, visualization results confirm that the fine-grained opinion adjustment mechanism enhances model interpretability.

papers.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of fine-tuning in financial NLP: The case of Social Trading Action Detection
papers.authors: D’Amico S., Maurino A., Osborne F., Sperlì G.
papers.abstract: Financial Natural Language Processing crucially leverages social media for market insights. However, most existing methods for this purpose rely on simple sentiment analysis models, which fail to capture the concrete trading intentions expressed in these discussions. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative to simplistic sentiment analysis, the actual benefits of fine-tuning across different model families remain unclear in noisy, domain-specific contexts like online forums. To address this gap, we present a comprehensive assessment of the advantages and limitations of fine-tuning for Social Trading Action Detection (STAD), a novel task that aims to classify online posts into actionable categories, namely buy, sell, or other. In addition, we introduce FinReddit-2K, a manually annotated dataset consisting of 2123 Reddit posts, designed to serve as a benchmark for this task. Our experimental analysis goes beyond standard performance metrics and identifies both the types of errors that fine-tuning can successfully mitigate and those that it may inadvertently introduce. Through a systematic evaluation of 57 models, comparing 14 traditional models with 23 zero-shot LLMs and 20 fine-tuned variants, our results show that fine-tuning yields an average F1-score improvement of ＋15.1%. The best-performing model, a fine-tuned Mistral-7B, achieves an F1-score of 86.0%, although our analysis reveals that fine-tuning fails to produce meaningful performance gains in several scenarios.

papers.title: Learning general-purpose and robust representations of microservice system states from multi-modal data
papers.authors: Xu Y., Ge J., Wu Y., Ma Y., Li H., Wu B., Li T.
papers.abstract: Microservice systems generate fragmented and misaligned multi-modal data, including metrics, logs, and traces, posing a major challenge for AIOps, which requires coherent system-state representations for downstream analytics. Existing approaches typically model spatio-temporal relations at a coarse granularity or are tailored to specific tasks, limiting their generalizability across different O&M scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose M3RL, a unified pre-training and fine-tuning framework for learning robust and transferable system-state representations. At its core, the spatio-temporal network (STNet) performs fine-grained semantic fusion of multi-modal data along both temporal and spatial dimensions and models evolving communication-driven dependencies among services. We further pre-train STNet with three complementary objectives: denoising reconstruction for robustness, future prediction for temporal evolution modeling, and causal contrastive learning for node-level discriminability. Extensive experiments on two public benchmark datasets demonstrate that M3RL consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art baselines across key downstream tasks, reducing state prediction MAE by 1.9%, increasing anomaly detection F1 by 4.7%, and improving root cause localization HR@1 by 4.8% on average. These results show that M3RL provides a robust and transferable representation backbone for multiple AIOps tasks.

papers.title: A mechanistic interpretability perspective on personality in large language models
papers.authors: Dan Y., Yu L., Lin J., Chen Q., Zhou J., Tian J., Bai Q., He L.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly reported to exhibit stable personality-like behaviors under standardized psychometric evaluations such as the Big Five, yet how such behaviors arise from internal computation remains unclear. In this work, we take a mechanistic perspective and aim to characterize how Transformer computation paths give rise to personality-consistent behavior. To enable this analysis, we introduce TraitTrace, to our knowledge the first dataset specifically designed for mechanistic studies of personality in LLMs, comprising 1800 human-curated situational prompts for circuit discovery and validation. Our analysis shows that personality-consistent behaviors are supported by compact circuits that involve only a small fraction of model components, rather than being diffusely distributed across the network. Across Llama2-7B-Chat and Phi-2, the extracted personality circuits achieve near-full-model Hit@10 performance, with an average score of 0.99, while retaining, on average, only about 8% of nodes and fewer than 0.05% of edges for each trait and level. Structural analyses reveal that high and low levels of the same trait are implemented by circuits that share similar nodes but differ in routing. Additionally, we find that Neuroticism exhibits comparatively lower cross-trait overlap, consistent with prior psychometric observations that it is less correlated with other Big Five traits. Furthermore, causal intervention experiments reveal that a small number of early-layer nodes act as bottlenecks that disproportionately govern personality expression. Together, these results provide a circuit-level account of personality in LLMs, bridging behavioral assessment and mechanistic interpretability, and suggesting new directions for more interpretable and targeted personality control and alignment.

papers.title: From chat to process: A conversational agent framework for social business process management
papers.authors: Sarr L.A., Barthe-Delanoë A.M., Bork D., Ayite K., Macé-Ramète G., Bénaben F.
papers.abstract: Traditionally, Business Process Management (BPM) approaches have been designed for repetitive, structured processes. With Volatile, Uncertain, Complex, and Ambiguous (VUCA) environments came a high context-dependence and an increased need for knowledge in processes. That led to more and more semi-structured and unstructured processes, which resulted in a shift from BPM to dynamic BPM, ambidextrous BPM, and even social BPM. Social BPM could be an answer to the rigidity of traditional BPM approaches when organizations operate in VUCA environments if context-sensitive tool support is given. In this paper, a proposition of a framework that combines AI conversational agents and social BPM is presented to help bring added agility to BPM. These agents are thought and designed to intervene by guiding, recommending best practices, and giving feedback; therefore, acting as participants in processes. Their roles go from co-constructing and structuring processes to supervising the execution of said processes through helping with task accomplishment. This framework is being developed using an exploratory approach that combines insights from the literature, a deductive design process, and evaluation through a representative use case. By combining BPM, AI, and social media, this framework could offer possibilities in these domains and help to increase agility in BPM.
