papers.title: Every bird has its nest: Boosting graph convolutional network via hierarchical learning
papers.authors: Liu G., Meng Q., Li C., Zhao Z.
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various graph analyzing tasks. They follow the message-passing paradigm, learning node representations by iterative aggregation of neighborhood information. The existing studies have explored various interesting techniques to boost the performance of GNNs, including initial residual, identity mapping, feature fusion, weighted aggregation, etc. However, most of them leverage the uniform message-passing radius for information aggregation, which results in a limited receptive field and impairs the ability of the model to capture dependencies at varying distances. To address this limitation, a novel HieRarchical Graph Convolutional Network (HieRaGCN) is proposed, which distributes each node into an optimal message-passing radius for hierarchical-aware graph representation learning. Specifically, it employs eigenvector centrality to quantify node importance, which is the foundation for hierarchical learning. Then, it designs two optional partitioning schemes (i.e., adaptive partitioning and hardcoded partitioning) to map various nodes into the ideal receptive field. Furthermore, it devises an innovative vertical loss to enrich the distinctiveness of features across various receptive fields. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that HieRaGCN achieves consistent improvements, outperforming baseline methods by 2.07%∼[jls-end-space/]4.10% in node classification and 0.56%∼[jls-end-space/]2.55% in link prediction. The source codes of this work are publicly available at https://github.com/ZZY-GraphMiningLab/HieRaGCN.

papers.title: Scientific hypothesis prediction based on large language models and causal graphs
papers.authors: Ba Z., Zhang Y., Bai R.
papers.abstract: Scientific hypotheses connect known facts with unknown possibilities. This study proposes a novel approach for scientific hypothesis prediction by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with causal graphs. Using a corpus of over 60,000 academic publications, we extracted 115,484 structured causal variable pairs through a comparative analysis of 18 groups of LLMs. We then constructed a Causal Claim Network (CCN) to capture implicit causal relationships in the literature. Building on this network, we introduce LLMCCN, a hypothesis-inference algorithm. Unlike existing hypothesis-prediction approaches, LLMCCN jointly identifies independent and dependent variables, traces effect pathways, and pinpoints mediating and moderating mechanisms. It therefore yields interpretable causal propositions rather than mere link predictions. Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations show that LLMCCN surpasses existing baselines. The evaluations also show that it outperforms AI-only baselines in novelty and helpfulness, and that its effectiveness is further enhanced with the assistance of domain experts. To validate the generated hypotheses, we conducted a large-scale empirical case study by analyzing 47,181 annual reports and > 710,000 publicly disclosed invention patents. Rigorous econometric analyses confirmed the statistical significance of most findings at the 1% level. These results validate the theoretical novelty and practical relevance of our inferred hypotheses. This study offers an efficient and scalable framework for automated and interpretable hypothesis discovery.

papers.title: CA-DE: Heterogeneous component-aware and antagonistic dependency-enhanced dual paths for long-term time series forecasting
papers.authors: Liu X., Li W., Liu F., Pan Q.
papers.abstract: Time series forecasting is widely applied in real-world scenarios. However, existing methods typically employ a unified architecture within a shared feature space, resulting in coupled representations that limit forecasting performance. To address this issue, we propose the CA-DE (Component-Aware and Dependency-Enhanced), a dual-path framework that decouples feature modeling along the temporal and variable dimensions. Along the temporal path, CA-DE employs time component awareness to hierarchically abstract low-frequency trends and reconstruct multi-period high-frequency seasons, thereby capturing long-term dependencies and cyclical phase patterns, facilitating targeted modeling of heterogeneous time components. Along the variable path, CA-DE employs a dependency enhancement mechanism that reverses variable sequences to construct antagonistic dependency channels, enabling explicit modeling of negative correlations between variables. It then independently integrates the bidirectional dependency features between variables outside the time feature space, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to express complex inter-variable dependencies. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that CA-DE achieves strong performance across multiple domain-specific forecasting tasks. Notably, on the Exchange dataset, CA-DE reduces MSE and MAE by 26.9% and 13.6%, respectively, highlighting its effectiveness and generalization ability for long-term time series forecasting.

papers.title: A secure federated feature selection framework for horizontally distributed medical data
papers.authors: Abdulsalami A.O., Gharehchopogh F.S., Abdullahi M., Elaziz M.A., Hassoon B.A., Xiong S.
papers.abstract: Feature selection is important for reducing dimensionality of medical data that is distributed across institutional silos. Existing federated feature selection (FFS) techniques, including evolutionary or population based methods, still suffer from local optima, slow convergence, and limited privacy protection. We propose a secure and robust framework for feature selection over horizontally partitioned medical data. Specifically, we introduce Binary Heterogeneous Comprehensive Learning Symbiotic Organism Search (BHCLSOS) and its federated extension (FBHCLSOS). In FBHCLSOS, each client runs BHCLSOS locally, and a central server computes mutual information (MI) from ɛ[jls-end-space/]-differentially private contingency tables uploaded by the clients. These statistics form informative feature groups that guide and refine the clients’ search in future rounds, which improves the quality of feature subsets without exposing raw data or statistics. BHCLSOS is further improved with reverse-bit and forward-bit mutation to preserve population diversity and reduce feature selection bias. Experiments on 15 public medical datasets with a KNN classifier show that FBHCLSOS outperforms several state-of-the-art FFS methods in terms of accuracy and F1-score under strict privacy constraints. The Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on 135 pairwise comparisons indicate that FBHCLSOS is significantly better in 110 cases (Formula presented), with the remaining comparisons being statistical ties and no losses ((Formula presented) ). This consistent dominance indicates that FBHCLSOS reliably extracts more relevant features than its peer competitors. A scalability study conducted as part of the experiments shows only minor accuracy degradation when the federation size grows, which indicates that FBHCLSOS can scale well to larger multi-institutional deployments.

papers.title: Explicit token modeling and hierarchical feature reasoning for multimodal fake news detection
papers.authors: Jia Y., Chen H., Shi Z., Yang X.
papers.abstract: Fake news dissemination poses serious challenges to information credibility, making multimodal fake news detection an important research problem. However, many existing methods rely heavily on implicit global alignment and encoders’ final-layer global representations, which can blur fine-grained token-patch correspondences and overlook semantic cues that emerge across intermediate layers, ultimately limiting detection performance. In this paper, we propose EMHR, a unified framework that couples explicit cross-modal consistency modeling with hierarchical semantic reasoning. Specifically, Explicit Token Modeling embeds token-patch consistency directly into cross-modal fusion, enabling the detector to capture subtle semantic mismatches that may be missed by implicit alignment. Moreover, Hierarchical Feature Reasoning progressively exploits intermediate textual representations to track semantic evolution across layers, providing fine-grained reasoning complementary to final-layer features. At the decision level, Confidence-Adaptive Feature Fusion aggregates multi-branch predictions via confidence-aware weighting, yielding more stable and discriminative outputs. Extensive experiments on Weibo17, Politifact, and GossipCop demonstrate the effectiveness of EMHR, delivering a 2.6% accuracy improvement on GossipCop over the strongest competing method and highlighting its superior ability to capture fine-grained cross-modal semantic discrepancies.

papers.title: Towards higher quality and fewer hallucinations: A multi-agent collaboration framework for LLMs
papers.authors: Shen S., Sun D., Qin Z., Su Y., Zhu L., Lu J., Huang Z., Wang S.
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in natural language tasks, single-agent architectures face an inherent optimization conflict between maximizing generative response quality and mitigating factual hallucinations. To address this, we propose the Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework (MA-CF), a structured prompt-driven pipeline that decomposes generation into distinct phases of drafting, parallelized evaluation, and final synthesis. By architecturally decoupling factuality verification from linguistic assessment into separate agent roles, MA-CF empirically mitigates the suboptimal trade-offs and consensus biases observed in both monolithic single-agent systems and traditional multi-agent debate frameworks. We evaluated MA-CF using small-scale backbones (Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B) against single-agent baselines, iterative debate architectures, and large-scale models across three datasets: PreciseWiki ((Formula presented) ), LongWiki ((Formula presented) ), and HaluEval 2.0 ((Formula presented) ). Experimental results demonstrate substantial quantitative improvements. On the LongWiki dataset, MA-CF increased Llama3.1-8B’s Recall@32 from 15.38% to 35.22% and F1@32 from 22.63% to 44.22%. On the cross-domain HaluEval 2.0 benchmark, the framework improved the Average Factual Rate from 65.24% to 73.28%. Furthermore, on the PreciseWiki dataset, MA-CF significantly improved the model’s ability to reject unanswerable queries, effectively reducing the probability of model error. Significantly, our findings confirm that a strategic ensemble of 8B-parameter models can match or surpass the hallucination mitigation capabilities of 671B-parameter models (e.g., DeepSeek-V3), offering a computationally efficient architecture for deploying reliable LLM systems in resource-constrained information environments.

papers.authors: Chen S., Liu Y.
papers.abstract: We introduce HPR-GenRM, a hierarchical process-level generative reward model for robust large language model (LLM) alignment in offline reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) settings, unifying long-horizon reasoning with explicit step-by-step verification through a three-tier architecture. Training on 25K hierarchically-annotated instances from HelpSteer2, MATH, and CodeContests, our Llama-3-8B-based model achieves 82.3% accuracy on RM-Bench (7.2% improvement over state-of-the-art), 89.1% step accuracy on MATH-500 with error localization F1 of 0.83, and 61% relative reduction in undetected adversarial attacks. Integration into RLHF yields 58.3% win rate on AlpacaEval2 (11.1% gain) while reducing policy-level reward hacking from 15% to 5%. This work presents hierarchical process-level reasoning as an effective approach for interpretable reward modeling within offline reward labeling and quality-sensitive alignment settings.

papers.title: BJZM: A scalable framework for developing and benchmarking LLMs with an open leaderboard in Chinese literature
papers.authors: Hu G., Wang K., Wang Q., Wang Q., Peng M.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in generative AI, large language models (LLMs) still struggle with Chinese literature. This literature is rich in artistry, history, culture, and emotion. Data scarcity and linguistic complexity limit LLMs’ domain-specific effectiveness. To address this, we propose BJZM, an open-source framework for Chinese literary LLMs. It integrates data, modeling, and evaluation into a unified ecosystem. BJZM has three key components. ChnLid is a diverse literary instruction dataset covering 6 tasks and 11 datasets, totaling 686K samples. BaiJia is a fine-tuned LLM available in 7B and 20B versions. ZhengMing is a benchmark with unseen datasets for robust evaluation. Experiments show that existing LLMs vary in performance. BaiJia generalizes well and excels in knowledge understanding and sentiment parsing. It rivals ChatGPT on several tasks. ZhengMing supported an evaluation workshop with 89 teams, many of which surpassed ChatGPT, demonstrating BJZM’s potential to advance literary AI. By providing data resources and an open leaderboard, BJZM facilitates research and promotes global appreciation of Chinese literary heritage. papers.title: Farsi Natural Language Processing: A Survey
papers.authors: Bokaei Z., Magdy W., Webber B.
papers.abstract: Variants of Persian (Farsi, Dari, and Tajiki) are spoken by more than 110 million people worldwide. Despite the growing interest in broadening the coverage of Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods, Persian has received limited attention. This survey addresses this gap by reviewing over 200 peer-reviewed studies published across the last two decades, documenting more than 40 publicly available corpora, and analysing linguistic challenges, pipelines, and applications across approaches ranging from rule-based methods to Large Language Models (LLMs). Given the rapid advancement of LLMs, we study the state of Persian-specific models across different tasks, review the available LLMs for Persian, assess their performance and limitations, and provide a comprehensive discussion of their strengths and gaps. Our analysis shows that although attention to Persian NLP has increased and notable progress has been made, critical gaps remain—particularly the scarcity of standardised benchmarks and gold corpora in tasks such as toxicity and safety, bias and fairness, and explainability and reasoning. Future progress requires expanding culturally grounded datasets, establishing robust evaluation frameworks, and fostering open-source collaboration and shared-task participation to accelerate the development of Persian NLP.

papers.title: A transferable attack framework for face impersonation with surrogate ensemble and semantic guidance
papers.authors: Song R., Tian Y., Li M.
papers.abstract: Face recognition systems (FRS) have achieved remarkable progress in real-world applications but they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples. Such attacks manipulate benign face images to mislead deployed FRS, posing risks to identity authentication, financial assets, and personal security. However, existing face attack methods often transfer poorly across models and insufficiently exploit target-identity semantics, especially in impersonation attack tasks. To address these limitations, we propose S2[jls-end-space/]FA, a transferable multimodal framework for face impersonation attacks that integrates semantic guidance with a scaled model ensemble strategy. S2[jls-end-space/]FA employs a diffusion-based generator conditioned on textual prompts and visual features to produce semantically guided adversarial face candidates. A Grad-CAM-based semantic projector further localizes identity-relevant regions and constrains perturbation injection, while a scaled surrogate ensemble strategy improves cross-model transferability. These components are jointly optimized through a multi-objective loss that combines adversarial embedding similarity, CLIP-based semantic alignment, and perceptual regularization, thereby improving attack success while preserving visual fidelity. Experiments on benchmark datasets and multiple FRS show that S2[jls-end-space/]FA outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 20% improvement in attack success rate in the best case. Ablation studies and additional analyses further confirm the contribution of each component.

papers.title: Enhancing decision boundaries in continual learning through a decoupled Gaussian framework
papers.authors: Feng Z., Chen C., Yang Z., Yu L., Kuang P., Zhou M., Dang K., Gao Z., Ju Y.
papers.abstract: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to acquire new knowledge while retaining previously learned information. CNN-based and prompt-based CL methods have achieved remarkable progress in recent years. However, most prior work has primarily focused on reducing forgetting from the perspective of the model itself. In this paper, we investigate CL from the perspective of decision boundaries, analyzing the impact of instance-level feature overlap. To address this issue, we propose a generic Decoupled Gaussian Softmax Classifier that enhances class discriminability during CL process. Specifically, we decouple the features extracted by the backbone into multiple Gaussian distributions, which are directly fused into the feature space through weighted integration. A regularization term is introduced to penalize the overlap of similar features, while an adaptive decision boundary is assigned to each class to encourage inter-class separation and intra-class compactness. Experiments on 4 widely used continual learning datasets and 12 CL scenarios show that our method has good plug-and-play capability. It improves the average accuracy by 1%–2.63% over the baseline models, while effectively reducing both the forgetting rate and the Expected Calibration Error. papers.title: Boosting multimodal CoT reasoning through DPO with Error-prone Sample Synthesis
papers.authors: Lou Y., Ke W., He Y., Wang P., Liu Q., Xu H.
papers.abstract: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (MCoT) reasoning extends CoT by incorporating visual evidence into structured textual rationales, enabling more accurate and coherent step-by-step reasoning in multimodal scenarios. However, MCoT methods still face two major challenges: (1) error propagation, where a single flawed intermediate step can derail the final answer, and (2) over-reasoning, where unnecessarily long chains on simple or mismatched problems induce hallucinations. To address these challenges, we propose Critic-MCoT, a unified adversarial framework for step-wise multimodal CoT alignment. Specifically, (1) to prevent error propagation, we introduce a step-wise adversarial process that synthesizes plausible error-prone samples and yields (win, lose) pairs for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and (2) to mitigate over-reasoning, we train stage-specific LoRA modules via DPO, forming an integrated reasoning module that adaptively handles diverse problem complexities. Experiments on both science and math benchmarks are conducted using 2.5 K science and 2.5 K math training instances to synthesize error-prone samples. Evaluation is performed on 4.2 K science test instances and 9.5 K math test instances in total. On ScienceQA, Critic-MCoT improves over the strongest MCoT baselines by 2.65% (3B) and 4.72% (7B) in average accuracy; on multimodal math benchmarks, it further improves the weighted average accuracy by 4.59% (3B) and 6.02% (7B). Moreover, after training, the average normalized error rate across six error types is reduced by approximately 10.7% in relative terms.
